conventions.convention: Time runs over the integers; BX_t=X_{t-1}. The AR polynomial is φ(z)=1−Σφ_jz^j and the MA polynomial is θ(z)=1+Σθ_jz^j. Common factors are cancelled and both constant terms normalized to one before applying the root criteria.
White noise is centered, has common finite strictly positive variance, and is uncorrelated at distinct times; independence and identical distributions are additional assumptions.

Causal and inverse representations use one-sided absolutely summable coefficient sequences starting at zero, with almost-sure and L² filter interpretations. Their root criteria exclude zeros throughout the closed unit disk.

The covariance convention is γ(h)=Cov(X_{t+h},X_t). Spectral measures represent it using exp(ihλ); angular Lebesgue measure has total mass 2π, giving the density factor σ²/(2π). The spectral theorem assumes Countable Choice and excludes only unit-circle zeros of φ.

The sample-mean CLT assumes AC, iid centered innovations and Σ√(j+1)|ψ_j|<∞. A zero limiting variance is permitted; studentization requires a separately consistent nonnegative estimate of a strictly positive variance.

OLS uses fixed p≥1, optionally includes an intercept, and assumes AC, strict stationarity, canonical-shift ergodicity, past-independent iid innovations and a finite positive-definite regressor Gram matrix. Singular-design estimates and exceptional Wald statistics are set to zero.

load_bearing.statement: For a centered real weakly stationary process Z and c∈ℓ¹(ℤ), c(B)Z is well-defined almost surely and in L², centered and weakly stationary, with γ_Y(h)=Σ_{j,k}c_jc_kγ(h−j+k). Absolutely summable filters compose by convolution. The argument uses no choice axiom.

Defines centered positive-variance uncorrelated white noise, absolutely summable causal linear processes, normalized coprime ARMA equations, and absolutely summable causal and invertible representations.

For a weakly stationary solution of a normalized coprime ARMA equation driven by white noise of positive variance, an absolutely summable causal representation exists iff φ has no zero in |z|≤1; an absolutely summable invertible representation exists iff θ has no zero there. The coefficients are uniquely determined by θ/φ and φ/θ respectively, and the causal coefficients decay exponentially.

Under AC and the stated fixed-order AR, strict-stationarity, ergodicity, iid innovation, past-independence and finite positive-definite Gram hypotheses, √n(β̂_n−β) converges to N_d(0,σ²Γ⁻¹), the residual mean square converges in probability to σ², and the specified Wald statistic converges to χ²_d.

Under AC, weighted absolute coefficient summability and two-sided iid centered innovations of finite positive variance, √n(X̄_n−μ) converges to N(0,σ²Ψ²), where Ψ=Σψ_j. If σ²Ψ²>0 and a nonnegative variance estimate is consistent, the stated studentized statistic converges to N(0,1) and its symmetric intervals have the stated limiting coverage.

Assume Countable Choice. A real weakly stationary solution of the normalized coprime ARMA equation with centered positive-variance white noise has spectral density f(λ)=σ²|θ(exp(−iλ))|²/(2π|φ(exp(−iλ))|²) if φ has no unit-circle zero. No causal or invertible root condition is required.

seams_checked.note: The supplier page and its stationarity and autocovariance definitions agree with the consumer's finite-moment, shift-invariance and γ(h)=Cov(X_{t+h},X_t) conventions. The consumer does not infer a CLT or ergodic limit from weak stationarity or covariance summability.

The supplier page and spectral definition use angular measure of mass 2π, positive Fourier exponent for covariance representation and finite positive Radon spectral measures. The consumer preserves these conventions and the Countable Choice premise, constructing its density directly without importing Herglotz existence or periodogram inference conclusions.
